vocabulary.source_context: Thomas describing Chiayi: 嘉義沒有大都市的熱鬧，卻多了一股悠閒的氛圍

卻.meaning: yet/however — sits inside the second clause, not at the start like 但是

vocabulary.semantic_note: More elegant than 但是. Compressed concession — the 雖然...但是 pattern in a single word. Very natural in written Taiwanese Mandarin.

vocabulary.source_context: 嘉義沒有大都市的熱鬧 — Chiayi doesn't have a big city's bustle
vocabulary.semantic_note: One of those untranslatable Chinese concepts — 'bustling' is close but misses the warmth. Hot noise: night markets, temple festivals, family reunions. Positive energy.

vocabulary.source_context: 卻多了一股悠閒的氛圍 — yet has more of a leisurely atmosphere
vocabulary.semantic_note: Very Taiwanese flavor. The 悠 is the same character from Moon's Ci poetry 水悠悠 — there it meant 'flowing endlessly,' here it means 'easygoing.' Same underlying energy of unhurried drift.

vocabulary.source_context: 一股悠閒的氛圍 — a strand of leisurely atmosphere
vocabulary.semantic_note: The air that surrounds you. More literary than 氣氛 (qìfēn) which is the more common spoken form — both mean atmosphere but 氛圍 has a softer, more descriptive quality.

vocabulary.english: a strand/whiff/current of (measure word for intangibles)
vocabulary.source_context: 多了一股悠閒的氛圍 — has more of a strand of leisurely atmosphere
vocabulary.semantic_note: Measure word for things you can sense but not hold: feelings, scents, currents, vibes, forces. You wouldn't say 一個氛圍, you'd say 一股氛圍.
related_words: 一陣 (yī zhèn, a burst of)
一種 (yī zhǒng, a kind of)

vocabulary.source_context: 之前每個月都會去露營 — before, every month would go camping
vocabulary.semantic_note: Literally 'dew-camp' — sleeping under the open sky. Camping culture is huge in Taiwan, especially in the mountainous central regions. 露 is also a 多音字: lù (dew/expose) vs. lòu (to reveal/leak). Here it's lù.

vocabulary.source_context: 會去蠻多台灣的其他地方旅行 — would travel to quite a lot of other places in Taiwan
vocabulary.semantic_note: Distinctly Taiwanese. Mainland equivalent is 挺多 (tǐng duō) or 很多. 蠻 as 'quite/pretty' is one of the strongest 台灣味 markers — hearing it is like hearing 'reckon' and knowing someone is Southern. Pattern is productive: 蠻好 (pretty good), 蠻有趣 (quite interesting), 蠻遠 (quite far).
related_words: 挺多 (tǐng duō, quite a lot — mainland equivalent)
很多 (hěn duō, a lot — neutral)

vocabulary.source_context: 蠻多台灣的其他地方 — quite a lot of other places in Taiwan
vocabulary.semantic_note: 其他 is a clean, high-utility modifier meaning 'other/else.' Works with anything: 其他人 (other people), 其他問題 (other questions), 其他時間 (other times). 地方 is one of the most useful nouns in Chinese.
related_words: 其餘 (qíyú, the rest — more formal)

vocabulary.source_context: 也去了台湾差不多一年 — went to Taiwan for about a year
vocabulary.semantic_note: Literally 'differs not much' — the gap is small. Extremely high frequency. Works as an adverb (差不多一年, about a year), adjective (都差不多, all roughly the same), and even a standalone response (差不多吧, more or less).
related_words: 大概 (dàgài, roughly — slightly more formal)

vocabulary.source_context: 还没去过德国 — haven't been to Germany yet
vocabulary.semantic_note: 还 adds the 'yet' — implying the action is expected to happen eventually. Just 没 is flat negation (didn't); 还没 is 'not yet' (but someday). Crucial distinction for conveying intent vs. finality.

vocabulary.source_context: 西班牙、法国、比利时、荷兰和英国 — listing countries with 、
vocabulary.semantic_note: The Chinese list comma — used specifically to separate items in a series. Regular comma (逗号 dòuhào) is for clauses, 顿号 is for lists. Small punctuation detail that makes your Chinese look noticeably more literate.

vocabulary.source_context: 对了，我不太常上这个网站 — by the way, I don't get on this site much
vocabulary.semantic_note: Natural topic-shifter in conversation. Literally 'right!' as if something just occurred to you. Way more natural than 顺便说一下 (shùnbiàn shuō yīxià) which sounds textbook-stiff.
related_words: 順便 (shùnbiàn, by the way — more formal)

vocabulary.english: not too often, not very frequently
vocabulary.source_context: 我不太常上这个网站 — I don't get on this site too often
vocabulary.semantic_note: Softer than 不常 (not often) — the 太 hedges it, making it sound less absolute. Like 'not all that often' vs. 'rarely.' Pattern is productive: 不太好 (not too good), 不太贵 (not too expensive), 不太远 (not too far).
related_words: 不常 (bù cháng, not often — stronger)

vocabulary.source_context: 欢迎加我 — welcome to add me (on WhatsApp)

迎.meaning: to greet, to meet, to receive

vocabulary.semantic_note: Literally 'joyfully greet.' Works both as a standalone (欢迎! Welcome!) and as a verb-complement (欢迎加我, welcome to add me; 欢迎来中国, welcome to come to China). Very warm and polite without being stiff.
related_words: 歡迎光臨 (huānyíng guānglín, welcome — formal, shop greeting)

grammar_patterns.note: Chinese uses BOTH halves, unlike English. Encountered in Michael's message.
examples: 雖然說繁體字我看的懂，但是我們這裡一般用簡體字

grammar_patterns.note: Comparison pattern. Michael comparing his English skills.
examples: 我英語寫作閱讀和翻譯比聽力口語好

grammar_patterns.english: describes how well something was done
grammar_patterns.note: 得 here is pronounced 'de' (neutral), NOT 'dé'. Different from 得到.

examples: 我對唐代越來越有興趣

grammar_patterns.note: 从 opens the bracket, 中 closes it. Everything between = the thing you're reaching into. 中 can be dropped but adds polish. Think of 从 as '(' and 中 as ')'. Works with any situation/experience as the filling.
examples: 从跟英语母语者聊天中得到什么 (get what from chatting with native English speakers)
从书中学到很多 (learned a lot from books)
从工作中得到快乐 (get happiness from work)

grammar_patterns.english: every [time period], would always [do something] (habitual past)
grammar_patterns.note: Expresses a past routine or habit. 會 here is 'would' (habitual), not 'can.' 都 reinforces the 'every single time' quality. 每 sets the frequency, 都會 confirms the regularity. Without 都, it's softer; with 都, it's 'without fail.'
examples: 之前每個月都會去露營 (before, every month would go camping — Thomas)
每天都會練習寫字 (every day would practice writing characters)
每年都會回台灣 (every year would go back to Taiwan)

tone_pairs.note: Same pinyin, different tone changes meaning entirely. 韓語 = Korean, 漢語 = Chinese.
